item: H5 - protected-field refusal, restart reconnection, planted failure
method: Each protected field is a real input on a real page, and every refusal is checked twice: the reply must not be ok, AND the input must still be empty when read back from the DOM. A refusal that still wrote the value would be worse than no refusal. A non-protected field on the same form is filled successfully, so 'refused' cannot be a broken fill wearing a safety label.
restartNote: Consent is durable; authentication is not. The pairing token is never persisted — it lives in memory only, so the token captured before the restart is rejected afterwards. What survives is the record that the user paired this origin, and the granted host permission. The reconnect therefore sends no secret at all, and receives a BRAND-NEW token that is verified to differ from the pre-restart one and to actually work. Persisting the token itself would have been the easy route and is explicitly forbidden by extension-protocol-parity.test.ts, because a stored bearer token outlives the pairing it belonged to.
plantedFailureNote: page.verify was asked to confirm a heading that says something the page does not say. Catching that is what makes every other verification in this series worth anything.
